To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pleasure and suffering in caring for the elderly in LTCIs is experienced by nursing workers in the context of the relationship between work, health and illness.
the pleasure and suffering are part of the daily life of nursing workers in LTCIs, and that the suffering can be reinterpreted to the benefit of the care provided to the elderly.
the pleasure and suffering are part of the work of nursing in LTCI, and that these feelings are related to the psychodynamics of work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of understanding the psychodynamics of work of professionals who take care of the elderly, as a way to improve the quality of life and the quality of care of these.
the identification of the situations that create the pleasure and suffering of nursing workers in LTCIs.
the understanding of the pleasure and suffering of the elderly institutionalization in the nursing workers perspective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nursing workers in LTCIs experience mixed feelings, which are related to the pleasure of being able to contribute to the clinical improvement and the creation of affective bonds with senior people, as well as the suffering of living with the resistant behavior of these, the estrangement of family and the death of elderly people.

the nursing workers' suffering and pleasure are related with their own subjectivity, with the subjectivity of their patients and with the subjectivity and the social context of the LTCI, which are the three dimensions of the Theory of Psychodynamics at Work.
the pleasure and suffering in nursing work with elderly people is related to the quality of the relationship between the worker and the patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pleasure and suffering are two faces of the same coin.
the pleasure and suffering are experienced as part of the work of the nursing professionals in LTCIs.
the suffering is the result of the lack of recognition by the senior people and the families, which leads the nursing workers to the feeling of being unappreciated.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pleasure and suffering are part of the work of the nursing professionals in the LTCI, and that the suffering is not only a feeling, but also an action, which is experienced by the worker in the care of institutionalized elderly people.

the pleasure and suffering are part of the daily life of nursing professionals in LTCI, and they can be managed by the institution through the implementation of policies and programs that promote the quality of life of the elderly and their workers.
we can understand that the pleasure in work is a result of the recognition of the workers by the elderly and vice versa.
